extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing responses to peer reviewers (academic researchers submitting manuscripts)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing a systematic, professional response-to-reviewers document and revised manuscript when resubmitting to a journal; includes how to interpret, prioritize, and address reviewer and editor comments. Aimed at helping authors improve acceptance chances while maintaining professionalism and ethical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consume reviewers’ critiques
rubrics_metrics.description: Value feedback; avoid personalizing critiques; regard feedback as opportunities for improvement; address critiques systematically and patiently; remain composed and evaluate each comment objectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: View feedback as a valuable opportunity to improve the work; do not perceive critical remarks as personal attacks; approach negative or major comments with a neutral, objective perspective; let feedback sit for a couple of days (‘sleep on it’) before responding; categorize comments as 'major' or 'minor' and store them securely to ensure careful consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read carefully and understand reviewers’/editor’s comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Thoroughly examine and categorize comments for clarity and understanding; break down comments into separate points; distinguish between positive feedback and critiques; address all points and number them accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully examine the editor’s letter and reviewers’ remarks to pinpoint emphasized points; take sufficient time to understand each comment and, if needed, break comments down; label and number each comment (e.g., Review 1, comment 1) and evaluate whether and how they can be addressed; the objective is to demonstrate commitment by meticulously addressing each comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek opinion (consult co‑authors and colleagues)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss reviewers’ comments with co-authors and colleagues to gain different perspectives and reach consensus on how to address comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brainstorm with the research group for ideas, especially on complex criticisms; obtain input from peers who may offer insights or suggested changes you had not considered; use these consultations to form a unified, considered response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize feedback: address major revisions first
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and prioritize major issues (scientific/methodological) before attending to minor clarifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major comments typically affect the manuscript’s core validity and should be handled first; revise and clarify significant points before fixing minor issues (e.g., wording, references, small data corrections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be polite and respectful; express gratitude
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain professionalism and gratitude toward reviewers; avoid confrontational or defensive tones even when disagreeing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express appreciation for reviewers’ time and input; apologize and clarify if reviewers misunderstood points (this often indicates unclear writing); do not respond rudely even if comments seem discourteous—preserve a constructive tone to improve chances of acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay attention to details: respond to every point raised
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure all points raised by reviewers are addressed individually, specifically, and thoroughly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a bullet contains multiple issues, answer each sub-point explicitly; provide requested data/figures or a supplement if needed; add or update references; delete unnecessary material or shorten sections (specify extent of reduction); make minor corrections (grammar/typography); avoid ignoring difficult points—be specific about limitations if something cannot be done.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be thorough and plan responses (organize systematically)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize and systematically respond to each reviewer comment with clear, detailed explanations and a professional format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number reviewers’ points and respond sequentially; provide specific, formal responses to every point; submit responses directly below the reviewers’ comments; tighten language and correct mistakes in the response and revised manuscript; where feasible, comply with reviewer requests; ensure clarity and professionalism throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start each response with a clear direct answer
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin each comment response with a clear and direct answer to the specific issue raised (a ‘yes’ or ‘no’ when possible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the direct answer, provide the supporting explanation, details of changes (with page/line references), or justification for refusal; this structure helps editors/reviewers quickly see whether the authors accepted the suggestion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid arguing every single comment; choose your battles
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not dispute all suggestions; only refute suggestions supported by valid reasons and evidence; justify refusals concisely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge the comment, then give a concise factual explanation for not implementing the suggestion; use evidence/references where relevant; be aware reviewers may tolerate only one refusal—repeated argumentation risks frustrating reviewers and jeopardizing publication; for substantial disputes, appeal to the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguous situations: request clarification and escalate appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Handle unclear, conflicting, or ethically concerning comments by seeking clarification or contacting the editor when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a comment is unclear, request clarification in the cover letter or by contacting the editor; when two reviewers conflict, examine both and choose the approach that best matches your vision, then explain to the editor why you followed one comment over another; report ethical concerns (e.g., suspected reviewer misconduct) separately to the editor and consider requesting a reviewer change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect the journal’s guidelines when accommodating reviewer requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If reviewers ask for additions that exceed journal limits, either implement with editor permission or justify refusal using the journal’s author guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adding material would violate limits, seek editor authorization before expanding content; if the request conflicts with the manuscript’s scope or the journal’s rules, write to the editor explaining why you cannot comply and justify your decision in the response letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight changes in the revised manuscript; make navigation easy
rubrics_metrics.description: Make it easy for reviewers and editors to find and verify changes by clearly indicating what was altered in the revised manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use typographical aids (track changes, colored fonts, highlights), or a table formatting with columns for reviewer comment, author response, and manuscript change with page/line references; copy reviewer comments and insert author responses below in a distinct color or font; if using multiple formats, clarify in the cover letter; be mindful that heavy markings can make the manuscript hard to read—provide clean and marked copies if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise and improve: document all corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure necessary corrections are made in the manuscript and that all changes are properly documented and highlighted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide both a version with changes highlighted and a clean version if the journal requires; follow submission requirements exactly; verify that changes match the responses in the response letter and that nothing was missed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review again: final proofreading and declare AI use if applied
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform a final thorough review of the revised manuscript; use language experts if needed and declare any AI tools used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If writing in a non-native language consider expert translation/proofreading; AI tools may help proofreading, but their use should be declared; carefully check for errors introduced by revisions before resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express gratitude again; include introductory and concluding paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin the response letter with appreciation for reviewers’ time and end by summarizing major changes and thanking reviewers and the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A brief introductory paragraph sets a positive tone; a concluding paragraph summarizing main revisions and reiterating gratitude closes respectfully; sample wording is provided in the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmit promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmit the revised manuscript and response materials quickly to keep the review process moving while comments remain fresh to reviewers and editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt resubmission with a detailed response letter, a clear response table, and highlighted changes demonstrates commitment and can increase the likelihood of acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid copying reviewers’ comments into the manuscript (plagiarism of reviewers’ comments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not directly copy-and-paste reviewers' comments into the manuscript; paraphrase reviewer suggestions and integrate them in your own words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directly pasting reviewers' text may raise academic integrity concerns; instead, incorporate useful suggestions by paraphrasing and reflecting the authors’ voice; this preserves originality while responding to feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change and modify where it makes sense; explain if outside scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement reviewer suggestions when they improve the manuscript; when a request falls outside the study’s scope, explain and justify the refusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reviewer asks for additional experiments or analyses that stray from the study objectives, explain why it is outside scope; provide a concise rationale in the response letter and, where appropriate, propose alternative, feasible amendments.
